title: The release gate passes a stale committed platform binary: compare a build or probe behaviour, not a checksum map against itself (DEC-204)
description:
DEC-204 (OPAG-1419), filed from the DEC-161 AC4 verification at dev b337381d on 2026-10-19. QCLI-438 is the HANDOFF RECORD for this defect, not the fix; this task is the fix. Publishing stays the operator (DEC-151).

DEFECT. The release gate (scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs) hashes each committed platform binary and compares the digest ONLY against a checksum map (manifest.questBinarySha256 and rootPackage.questPlatformPackages[...]) that is regenerated from those same committed binaries. The map therefore always agrees with the binaries, and nothing rebuilds from the current src/ and compares. A binary stale relative to src/ passes by construction.

MEASURED AT dev b337381d. The committed npm/quest-darwin-arm64/bin/quest blob f5702eb7 (sha256 59d1c0dc...) contains no --fields string. It answers `task view <id> --fields title` and `task list --fields id` with exit 2 (Unrecognized flag), while the same commands exit 0 from src/cli/main.ts at that SHA. The installed quest 0.13.0 binary is byte-identical to that committed blob, so published 0.13.0 lacks QCLI-312 and QCLI-291. QCLI-438 records the same class for QCLI-437: five of six committed binaries embed the pre-fix help string "--source <project>" while src/ has zero occurrences.

RULING (DEC-204). Replace the self-referential comparison with build-then-compare, or with a behavioural probe. For 0.14.0 the probe is: on the committed host-platform binary, `task view <id> --fields title` and `task list --fields id` must exit 0; the 0.13.0 binary must exit 2 on the same commands as the negative control in the same run. The fix must be proven both ways: a deliberately stale binary goes red, and a fresh build goes green.

SCOPE. Gate fix only; no release and no publish. QCLI-499 (release 0.14.0, quest half of the pair with lore-cli#572) is made a dependency of this task so the pair stays blocked behind it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A deliberately stale committed binary fails the release gate in a run that also passes a binary freshly built from the same source tree, so the gate is proven in both directions

For 0.14.0, the committed host-platform binary answers `quest task view <id> --fields title` and `quest task list --fields id` with exit 0, while the 0.13.0 binary exits 2 on the same commands as the negative control in the same run (behavioural-probe route), or the build-then-compare route demonstrates the identical stale-versus-fresh difference by building and comparing both
The gate no longer passes a binary solely because its digest matches a checksum map generated from that same committed binary, and the route chosen is recorded in the task final summary
QCLI-499 records a dependency on this task, so the 0.14.0 pair release is blocked until the gate is fixed

plan: 1. Add scripts/release-binary-probe.mjs: probe the committed host-platform binary with `task list --fields id` and `task view <id> --fields title`, asserting exit 0 and the projected shape; release-context enablement predicate.
2. Wire the probe into scripts/check-package-artifacts.mjs so the release gate refuses a binary that cannot answer the probes, while leaving source-gates green in the strings-first bump state.
3. Tests: injected stale (exit 2) versus fresh (exit 0) results prove the gate red and green in one run; no-probe-ran fails; enablement predicate.
4. Real both-ways proof: committed host binary (stale) fails, freshly compiled host binary passes, same run; record exit codes.
5. Update the release runbook and CHANGELOG; run bun run check under pinned 1.4.2 and lore check.
6. PR, CI green, dispatch-check, independent review, then hold before land.
